summary:
FlameSync is an interactive, full-stack combustion-research dashboard designed to evaluate spacecraft flammability risks. We developed a centralized platform that aggregates and normalizes over 1,330 disparate records from 11 different NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) spreadsheets into a unified visual explorer.

To address the challenge of making dense microgravity research actionable, FlameSync integrates three computational tools: a deterministic ranking engine to sort historical records against specific mission constraints, a Random Forest regression model to predict CFI-G experimental burn times, and a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) AI assistant that allows researchers to chat directly with indexed NASA research PDFs.

This project is important because it bridges the gap between raw aerospace data and applied engineering. By transforming fragmented, complex datasets into a deployable, high-contrast command center, FlameSync accelerates how engineers analyze fuel behaviors, oxygen fractions, and chamber pressures to ensure safer spaceflight operations.
details:
What it does and how it works: FlameSync is a comprehensive, full-stack combustion-research dashboard. It dynamically ingests and normalizes over 1,330 historical microgravity combustion records from 11 diverse NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) spreadsheets. The platform features an Explorer for filtering raw data, a Compare tool utilizing records for safety-space missions , a Ranking engine to sort records against mission constraints, a Machine Learning Predictor for CFI-G burn times, and an AI-powered Assistant that uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to answer questions directly from indexed NASA research PDFs.

Benefits and intended impact: Microgravity combustion data is incredibly valuable but often fragmented across varying schemas, file types, and research papers. FlameSync breaks down these data silos, transforming raw, dense metrics into a highly visual, actionable command center. The intended impact is to accelerate how aerospace engineers evaluate flammability risks such as oxygen fraction thresholds and chamber pressures ultimately contributing to safer spaceflight operations and habitat design.

Tools, coding languages, and software used:

  • Backend & Data Pipeline: Python, FastAPI, Pandas (for dynamic data parsing), and Scikit-learn (for the Random Forest regression model).
  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS.
  • AI & Database: ChromaDB (local vector database) and the OpenRouter API (for LLM RAG capabilities).

Creativity and team considerations: We merged chemical engineering first-principles with modern software architecture. When designing the pipeline, we carefully considered scientific integrity: rather than forcing mismatched data into a rigid table, our parser gracefully handles varying schemas by preserving the original source-row values alongside our normalized fields. Creatively, we designed the UI with a high-contrast, dark-mode "Space Operations" aesthetic to ensure critical metrics remain highly legible.
